## Hooks installed in this repo

- `PostToolUse` on test files — **blocks**: snapshots, fetch/axios mocks, `try/catch` without assert, `expect(fn())…toThrow` without the wrapper, loops/conditionals around `expect`, test-id/CSS locators and class-based visibility in component tests, fixed pauses in E2E, exported object fixtures. **Warns**: numbers in test names, `toHaveBeenCalled*`, `.only`/`.skip`, a mocked repository, chained act/assert groups, time without fake timers, selection/expansion state asserted through a CSS class (`toHaveClass('active')`) instead of the ARIA attribute. A blocked edit comes back with the list — fix the test, do not fight the hook; `// ninja-testing-ignore` with a reason is the escape hatch for a deliberate exception.
- `PreToolUse` — **denies** in Bash: snapshot updates (`-u`, `--update`), `--no-verify`, force push, changing Stryker thresholds from the command line, deleting test files. **Asks** before editing runner/mutation config files (when a test fails, the fix is in the test, not in the config) and before any edit that adds a `// Stryker disable` comment (excluding a mutant is a human's verdict); denies edits to `__snapshots__`.
- `Stop`: demands a **green** run of the **whole** suite (the configured command as a whole — not `test:e2e`, not one file, not `-t`) made **after your last change** (edits through the Edit tool, shell redirects, files a script wrote); in **strict** mode also mutation testing on the logic your tests cover and, once the report exists, a verdict on every surviving mutant (test gap / implementation boundary / equivalent) in your final message. At most two blocks per user turn.
